ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — John Henry Holliday Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Diagnosis of cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis: sputum, chest X-ray, baseline tests, public-health report, home isolation, and alcohol assessment with a safety assessment. Concerns: He wants to get back to his dental practice as soon as it is safe for his patients; He is frightened by the diagnosis and wants to know that it can be cured. [S]

tr.td: Isoniazid 300 mg tablet, one tablet daily
300 mg once daily by video-observed therapy with the health department, seven days a week, for six months
Rifampin 300 mg capsules, two capsules (600 mg) daily
600 mg once daily on an empty stomach by video-observed therapy with the health department, seven days a week, for six months
Pyrazinamide 500 mg tablets, three tablets (1500 mg) daily
1500 mg once daily by video-observed therapy with the health department, seven days a week, for the eight-week intensive phase
Ethambutol 400 mg tablets, three tablets (1200 mg) daily
1200 mg once daily by video-observed therapy with the health department, seven days a week, until susceptibility results return
Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) 50 mg tablet, one tablet daily
Chest X-ray, two views: right upper lobe consolidation with a 3 cm thick-walled cavity; no effusion or hilar enlargement
Chest X-ray, two views, at the end of treatment: cavity closed, with residual right upper lobe scarring; kept as the baseline for any future comparison

tr.td: Diagnosis of cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis: sputum, chest X-ray, baseline tests, public-health report, home isolation, and alcohol assessment with a safety assessment
Two-week follow-up on treatment with infectious diseases consultation
Five-week review: susceptibility results, release from isolation, and liver monitoring
End of the intensive phase: two-month sputum and the start of the continuation phase
Same-day sick visit for nausea and vomiting during tuberculosis treatment

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Infectious diseases consultation to confirm the regimen and plan monitoring for cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis in a man who drinks heavily

Standard treatment: isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for eight weeks, then isoniazid and rifampin for eighteen weeks, by video-observed therapy with the health department, with pyridoxine

Monitoring: monthly symptom and weight check, sputum smear and culture monthly until two consecutive cultures are negative, liver tests at two weeks and monthly because of alcohol, and vision checks while on ethambutol
Public health: same-day report to the local health department, home isolation until noninfectious, and a contact investigation of his household, coworkers, and patients led by the health department

Alcohol care: brief intervention at diagnosis, a goal of no alcohol during treatment, counseling with a substance-use counselor, medication offered, AUDIT-C at each visit, and a safety review with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at every visit
Complete 182 doses of treatment under video-observed therapy within six months
All 182 doses completed: 56 in the intensive phase and 126 in the continuation phase, with one dose held during a stomach illness and made up at the end
Sputum culture negative at two months
Two-month culture showed no growth, so the continuation phase stayed at four months
No alcohol during treatment, to protect his liver
Not fully met: no drinking for most of the six months, with one evening of heavy drinking at a party about three months into treatment; AUDIT-C 3 at the end
Return to work once he is no longer infectious
Released from home isolation after three negative sputum smears and back at work four weeks into treatment
Weight back to at least 64 kg by the end of treatment
65.5 kg at the end of treatment, from 58.0 kg at diagnosis

list.item: Independent; working full days until the cough and night sweats wore him down over the last month [S]
Alert, sharp, and dryly humorous; organized thought; no signs of intoxication or withdrawal [S]
Mood worried about his work and his health; PHQ-9 6; no thoughts of suicide or self-harm [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 1873-02-10: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. Routine outpatient care. A new serious diagnosis, isolation, and heavy drinking can raise suicide risk, so safety is reviewed at every visit. He saved the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in his phone. No firearm in the home [S]
